biography.plain_text: Carol II was King of Romania from 1930 to 1940, the son of King Ferdinand and Queen Marie. His private wealth included royal inheritances and investments. He ended parliamentary democracy by establishing a royal dictatorship, before territorial losses and collapsing support forced his abdication. He spent his final years in Portugal.
biography.html: Carol II was King of Romania from 1930 to 1940, the son of King Ferdinand and Queen Marie. His private wealth included royal inheritances and investments. He ended parliamentary democracy by establishing a royal dictatorship, before territorial losses and collapsing support forced his abdication. He spent his final years in Portugal.

confidence.reason: Official institutional history supports parentage, reign, dictatorship, abdication and Portuguese exile. Specific inheritance evidence and historical personal securities holdings support the modest wealth sentence; no unsupported sector or total fortune is stated.

long_biography.plain_text:
King Carol II made cultural patronage a substantial part of his public role. His foundation for literature and art published Romanian writers and awarded prizes and scholarships. A separate cultural foundation organised village centres, student teams and popular publications, extending its activities beyond the capital into rural communities.

Stamp collecting was a sustained personal interest. His collection included rare Moldavian issues and the Swedish Treskilling Yellow, a unique printing error he acquired in 1937. During exile he sold several major rarities, including the Treskilling Yellow and a Mauritius invitation envelope in 1950.
